text.p: Shopping centre operator Westfield Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday the company looked forward to a continuing strong performance with increased profits in the current 1996/97 (July-June) financial year.
However, Westfield said the Australian retail environment remained subdued and the general outlook for Christmas trading was cautious.
In late August, the company announced a 22 percent rise in 1995/96 (July/June) net profit to A$74.94 million. It said at the time it expected increased earnings in the current year.
Westfield chairman Frank Lowy told the annual meeting that recent investments in the United States should allow profits to grow and also pointed to Asian opportunities.

"There are good prospects for us increasing our presence in the Southeast Asian region. Our expertise in the management and development of retail property is being sought by local investors and developers, and we are currently examining a number of opportunities," Lowy said.
He said another new area of business was retail management at airports which is "a natural extension of our core activity of shopping centre management and development".
Westfield was currently retail manager of three airport terminals in the United States and was actively seeking other opportunities.

Lowy said the recently formed affiliate Westfield America Trust had allowed Westfield Holdings to extend its involvment in the dynamic U.S. retail property industry and this would provide a solid base for future earnings.

"We have been active in the United States for many years and now manage a total of 26 shopping centres including the 22 properties in the CentreMark portfolio in which Westfield Holdings has a major equity interest."
Lowy said the company had a long term development programme for these properties to maintain and enhance their value well into the next century.
"Unlike the current situation in Australia, consumer confidence in the U.S. is strong which augurs well for retailing going into the Christmas trading period."
